gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hiero: Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs is a plain sans with outward-pointing terminals and lowercase that climbs nearly to cap height. Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs sits under Flavors, whose stout, hairline-free strokes carry the playful shouting while the body keeps quietly out of the way.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Noto Sans Arabic reads clean and modern, with generous openings in its small letters and a pronounced x-height. Noto Sans Arabic would carry a long stretch of text comfortably beneath Flavors, whose letters look drawn with a fixed-width nib.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Flavors is loud, towering and a bit playful. Noto Sans Armenian answers in a sans with full, tall lowercase and inviting round letters, so if you only resize one, make the body text larger or smaller and leave the heading alone.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Flavors hums along at a constant line weight. Noto Sans Balinese gives it a plain sans partner with breathing room inside each curve and short ascenders, so the heading's chunky diagonals get all the attention.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Flavors draws every stroke as stout as a pipe cleaner. Noto Sans Bamum follows in a sans-serif with big open counters, so a long page of text feels modern and light after that thick, towering heading.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Flavors cuts every stroke to a single width and stands tall with whimsical authority. Noto Sans Bassa Vah is the best partner for that, a sans-serif whose dominant midsection and pliers-like open c make a contemporary counterweight.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-batak: Stout, towering, a little cheeky. Flavors has no thin strokes at all, while Noto Sans Batak, a sans-serif with its own tall lowercase and a wide e, shares that height but feels friendlier and more relaxed.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Flavors looks thin yet has no thinner parts anywhere, with diagonals as heavy as its stems. Noto Sans Bengali is a plain sans with capitals barely taller than lowercase, and its open mouths make a pleasantly modern foil.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Noto Sans Bhaiksuki has plump, rope-coiled lowercase and easy open apertures in a friendly sans-serif. Make Flavors small and its neon-tube thickness gets crowded.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Marker-traced strokes, big and cheerful. Flavors brings that towering whimsy, while Noto Sans Brahmi, a sans with a high mean line and open-ended curves, sits beside it feeling cooler and more contemporary.
